name: 1Password
tagline: Password manager for individuals and teams that need shared vaults, secure autofill, and administrative controls.
description: 1Password is a password manager for storing and using credentials across devices, with shared vaults and team administration on business plans. This profile focuses on practical fit and questions to validate before purchase. Current prices, plan limits, customer counts, ratings, and compliance scope are not independently verified here; confirm them in 1Password’s official documentation.
priceRange: Not independently verified — check official pricing
pros: Shared vaults can help teams manage access to credentials without passing passwords around in chat or documents.
Browser autofill and password generation can reduce repetitive credential handling when they work with a team's actual browsers and sign-in flows.
Travel Mode is a distinctive option to investigate for people who travel with devices containing sensitive work information.
Teams evaluating developer workflows can test the 1Password CLI and Secrets Automation against their deployment process.
cons: A paid subscription may be unsuitable for people or teams that require a permanently free password manager; compare current plans before migrating.
Moving from another manager takes planning: test imports, shared-vault permissions, passkeys, recovery, and offboarding before switching everyone.
Administrative controls and integrations vary by plan, so do not assume a feature is included until the vendor confirms it for the exact subscription.
Security tooling does not replace account recovery planning, phishing-resistant authentication where available, device security, or staff training.

features.name: Unlimited Password Storage
features.description: Store unlimited passwords, credit cards, notes, documents, and identities in encrypted vaults with automatic syncing across all devices

features.name: Secret Key Encryption
features.description: Unique 128-bit Secret Key combined with master password creates SRP-based zero-knowledge encryption that even 1Password cannot decrypt

features.name: Watchtower Breach Monitoring
features.description: Automated scanning of credentials against 100,000+ known data breaches with real-time alerts for compromised passwords and vulnerable services

features.name: Travel Mode
features.description: Remove sensitive vaults from devices with one click, then restore them later — no data leaves your device until you choose to re-enable access

features.name: Two-Factor Authentication
features.description: Built-in TOTP authenticator generates one-time codes for 2FA-enabled services, eliminating the need for a separate authenticator app

features.name: Passkey Management
features.description: Store and autofill passkeys for passwordless authentication across websites and apps, supporting the FIDO2/WebAuthn standard

features.name: Browser Extension
features.description: Autofill and auto-save credentials in Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge, and Brave with biometric unlock on supported devices

features.name: Desktop & Mobile Apps
features.description: Full-featured apps for Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android with offline vault access, biometric unlock, and cross-device sync

features.name: Admin Console
features.description: Centralized dashboard for managing users, groups, vaults, and policies with activity logging and security audit trails

features.name: SCIM Provisioning
features.description: Automatic user provisioning and deprovisioning via SCIM with Okta, Azure AD, OneLogin, and JumpCloud for lifecycle management

features.name: Single Sign-On
features.description: SAML 2.0 and OIDC-based SSO integration allows users to authenticate via their identity provider while 1Password manages vault access

features.name: Usage Reports
features.description: Audit logs showing who accessed which vaults, when passwords were rotated, and which items have been shared externally

features.name: Item Sharing
features.description: Share individual passwords, documents, or notes with external partners through time-limited share links with view-only access

features.name: Vault-Based Access Control
features.description: Organize credentials into vaults with per-vault user and group permissions, supporting department-level and project-level separation

features.name: Virtual Payment Cards
features.description: Generate virtual credit card numbers with merchant-specific limits for online purchases, masking real card details from vendors

features.name: CLI & Secrets Automation
features.description: Command-line interface and Connect server for injecting secrets into CI/CD pipelines, Docker containers, and infrastructure as code

features.name: Emergency Kit
features.description: Printable PDF containing account recovery details, Secret Key, and master password hints for regaining access after account lockout

features.name: Privacy Cards
features.description: Integration with Privacy.com to create single-use and merchant-locked virtual card numbers directly from the 1Password interface

content.title: Summary
content.body: 1Password is worth evaluating when a person or team wants passwords, passkeys, secure notes, and other sensitive items organized in encrypted vaults. For organizations, the decision is less about a headline score and more about whether sharing, permissions, onboarding, offboarding, recovery, and audit needs match the available plan. PilotStack has not independently tested every feature or verified current commercial terms for this profile; treat the points below as a buying checklist, not a lab-test result.

content.title: Where it may fit
content.body: Consider 1Password if several people need controlled access to shared credentials, employees use multiple browsers and devices, or developers need to manage secrets as part of their workflow. Travel Mode may also be relevant to people who cross borders with work devices. These are use cases to validate in a trial or demonstration, not a claim that every workflow is available on every plan.

content.title: Trade-offs to evaluate
content.body: Compare the total subscription cost with alternatives that offer a free tier or self-hosting options. Before choosing, confirm which administrative controls, identity-provider integrations, reporting features, and developer tools are included in the plan you would buy. Ask the vendor for written answers where a security or compliance requirement is contractual.

content.title: Security review checklist
content.body: Before rollout, review the vendor's current security whitepaper and trust documentation; confirm encryption and account-recovery design; check available multi-factor and passkey support; verify data-processing terms and any required certifications directly; and test how access is removed when an employee leaves. Do not infer a certification or legal compliance guarantee from a product feature list.

content.title: Migration checklist
content.body: Pilot the import with a small group. Check duplicate entries, shared credentials, attachments, passkeys, browser autofill, mobile access, emergency recovery, and permissions. Keep the previous manager available during a controlled transition, and document how you will revoke old sessions and recover access if the migration fails.

content.title: How to make the decision
content.body: Run the same short trial with 1Password and at least one alternative. Score each against your own requirements: daily autofill reliability, team sharing, administrator visibility, recovery, integration fit, accessibility, and total cost for the next year. Record which criteria were actually tested and which answers came from vendor documentation. Choose the tool that meets your must-haves with the least operational friction.

faqs.question: Does 1Password have a free plan?
faqs.answer: Plan availability and trial terms can change. Check 1Password's official pricing page for current individual, family, and business options before budgeting.

faqs.question: What should a business test before buying?
faqs.answer: Test shared-vault permissions, onboarding and offboarding, account recovery, multi-factor authentication, browser and mobile autofill, and the reporting or integrations required by your organization.

faqs.question: Is 1Password suitable for developers?
faqs.answer: It may fit teams that need to manage credentials and developer secrets. Confirm the current CLI and Secrets Automation capabilities, plan requirements, and how they integrate with your deployment environment.

faqs.question: Does 1Password guarantee compliance?
faqs.answer: Do not assume a tool alone makes an organization compliant. Review the vendor's current trust documentation and contractual terms, then confirm that they meet the controls and obligations relevant to your organization.

faqs.question: How should a team migrate from another password manager?
faqs.answer: Run a small pilot first. Validate imported records, shared access, attachments, passkeys, recovery, browser autofill, and offboarding before scheduling a wider rollout.

faqs.question: How does 1Password compare with Bitwarden?
faqs.answer: Compare the exact plans you would use, including team administration, self-hosting requirements, sharing, recovery, integrations, and total annual cost. A universal winner is not meaningful unless the tools are evaluated against the same requirements.

faqs.question: Are the rating and pricing figures on this page verified?
faqs.answer: No. PilotStack has not independently verified a current rating, review count, or price for this profile. Use the vendor's official site for current commercial details.
